problem_understanding.text: The root problem was that the baseline retryPayment implemented only a single attempt, returning failed for any non-success outcome regardless of temporary failure semantics. Input validation gates (integer maxAttempts 1-10, array outcomes of length 1-10 with valid strings) remain unchanged from baseline.

approach_summary.text: Replace single-attempt baseline with sequential iteration over outcomes, counting attempts and stopping on success or permanent failure, while preserving all input validation and existing payment APIs.

architecture_fit.text: Retry logic is isolated in retryPayment function with no side effects; existing payment routes and health endpoint remain unchanged, fitting the stateless HTTP server architecture.

correctness.text: All payment regression tests and most retry tests pass; however, retry-bounded fails because maxAttempts is not enforced, causing the attempt count to exceed the configured bound when more temporary outcomes exist than maxAttempts allows.

maintainability.text: Small, focused retryPayment function is readable, but missing bound enforcement is a maintainability risk; unit tests do not cover the bound case, and repository tests failing suggests coverage gaps.

problem_understanding.text: The baseline simulated only one attempt; the challenge requires bounded retries where temporary failures are retried up to maxAttempts, stopping on success or permanent failure.

solution_design.text: Implement sequential outcome loop with attempt counter, return success immediately, break on permanent, return failed after loop; input validation preserved; maxAttempts parameter accepted but not used to bound iterations.

strengths.text: Simple iterative design in retryPayment is easy to reason about and test.
Correctly handles success, permanent, and outcome-exhaustion cases.
Input validation for outcomes and maxAttempts is preserved from baseline.

tradeoffs.text: Simplicity of direct iteration trades off against missing maxAttempts bound enforcement.
Unit tests cover many cases but omit the bound scenario, reducing confidence in edge-case correctness.

unverified_assumptions.text: All outcomes in the array are meant to be consumed sequentially without randomization or concurrency.
maxAttempts is intended to cap attempts before outcomes are exhausted, not to mandate exactly that many attempts.
The rehearsal description stating maxAttempts is intentionally missing reflects a known partial implementation rather than a design decision for production.
